title: Barron's AP Statistics 2027 Quiz 11 — Unit 2
chinese_title: 巴朗 AP 统计 2027 Quiz 11

options.A: During half the weeks, the number of cloudy days is less than 2.73, and during half the weeks, the number of cloudy days is greater than 2.73.
options.B: The majority of weeks have either 2 or 3 cloudy days.
options.C: In any given sample of weeks, the average number of cloudy days per week will be 2.73.
options.D: The long-run average for number of cloudy days in a week is 2.73.

questions.stem: Over several years, data were collected on the number of cloudy days per week in a certain locale. The values varied from 0 to 7, and a distribution of relative frequencies was found. Let the random variable X represent the number of cloudy days in a week. The mean of X is 2.73. Which of the following statements is the best interpretation of the mean?
questions.answer_text: The expected value or mean is a long-term average. It is not a median. This value may not be the most likely value, and in this example, it can never occur. For any given sample, anything might result.

options.A: The average number of teacher absences per day is 4.31.
options.B: The long-term average number of teacher absences per day is 4.31.
options.C: On average, the number of teacher absences per day varies from the mean by 4.31.
options.D: In a random sample of days, the number of teacher absences per day is expected to be 4.31 away from the mean.

questions.stem: A high school principal records the number of teacher absences per day. Let the random variable Y represent the number of teacher absences in a given day. The standard deviation is 4.31. Which of the following statements is the best interpretation of the standard deviation?
questions.answer_text: The standard deviation gives the average or typical amount of variability from the mean for the population.

questions.stem: Let X denote the number of accidents in a 1-month period at a certain intersection. Suppose the probability distribution of X is shown in this table. X 0 1 2 3 4 P(x) 0.16 0.24 0.37 0.15 0.08 Which of the following would be evaluated to calculate the expected value of X?
questions.answer_text: The expected value or mean of a discrete random variable is given by ∑ xP(x). From the table, ∑ xP(x) = 0(0.16) + 1(0.24) + 2(0.37) + 3(0.15) + 4(0.08).

questions.stem: An insurance company charges $800 annually for car insurance. The policy specifies that the company will pay $1,000 for a minor accident and $5,000 for a major accident. If the probability of a motorist having a minor accident during the year is 0.2 and of having a major accident is 0.05, how much can the insurance company expect to make on a policy?

questions.stem: Suppose you are one of 7.5 million people who send in their name for a drawing with 1 top prize of $1 million, 5 second- place prizes of $10,000, and 20 third-place prizes of $100. Is it worth the $0.78 postage it costs you to send in your name?

In Skee-Ball, a player rolls a ball up a ramp and tries to land the ball in the holes with the greatest point values. One particular player has the following point distribution for any given roll. X (points) 10 20 30 50 100 Probability 0.50 0.25 0.15 0.05 0.05 Determine the expected value and interpret it in context.
questions.answer_text: ∑xP(x) = 10(0.50) + 20(0.25) + 30(0.15) + 50(0.05) + 100(0.05) = 22. This player will average 22 points per game in the long run. (Note that 22 points can never be the result of a single game.)

questions.stem: Suppose you are asked to play a game where you roll a single fair six-sided die. If it lands on 1 or 6, you win $5 and the game is over. If it doesn’t land on 1 or 6, you flip a fair coin, winning $1 for heads and $2 for tails, and the game is then over. Let X be the amount of money won. (a) Create a probability distribution for X. (b) What are the expected value and standard deviation for X? Interpret them in context. (c) How much money should you pay to play this game for it to be a fair game?
questions.answer_text: (a) The probability of 1 or 6 on the first roll is . The probability of 2, 3, 4, or 5 followed by a heads is . Similarly, the probability of 2, 3, 4, or 5 followed by a tails is 4 . 1 or 6 on first roll 2, 3, 4, or 5 and heads 2, 3, 4, or 5 and tails X (money won) $5 $1 $2 Probability (b) In the long run, a player will average winning about $2.67 per game. The player winnings for a randomly selected game will generally vary about $1.70 from the mean of $2.67. (c) To be a fair game, you should be willing to pay about $2.67.

questions.stem: A roulette wheel has numbers 1 through 36, half black and half red, plus two green numbers, 0 and 00. Suppose you plan to always bet $5 on “lucky” 13. If the ball lands on 13, you receive $175 back, otherwise nothing. Let X be the amount of money you are ahead after one spin of the wheel. (a) Create a probability distribution for X. (b) What are the expected value and standard deviation for X? Interpret them in context. (c) One day you quit when you’re over $100 ahead. What is the most likely number of games you played? Explain.
questions.answer_text: (a) If the ball lands on 13, the player is ahead $175 − $5 = $170. If the ball lands on anything other than 13, the player loses $5. X $170 −$5 P(x) (b) In the long run, you will average losing about $0.39 per game. Your winnings for a randomly selected game will generally vary about $28.01 from the mean of −$0.39. (c) To be over $100 ahead, you most likely played one game and won, rather than losing some number of games before winning.
